question.problem: Consider the thin plate $D$ enclosed between the curve $y=\sqrt{x}$ and the $x$-axis for $0\le x\le 4.$ Given that the area of the plate is $\frac{16}{3},$ find the $x$-coordinate of its centroid.
question.worked_solution:
The centroid of a lamina $D$ with area ${A}_{D}$ is given by $({x}_{c},{y}_{c}),$ where

$$
{x}_{c}=\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}x\,\,\text{d}A,\,{y}_{c}=\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}y\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that $D$ is a type I plane region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121640/assets/951eb7592df1645f8743817809c0d4604b779de6a3112f7fcaf6aca5f214f302.png)

So, we have 

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 4,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{x}}
$$

and ${A}_{D}=\frac{16}{3}.$

Therefore, the $x$-coordinate of the centroid is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{c} & =\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}x\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{3}{16}{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{16}{\int }_{0}^{4}x{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{16}{\int }_{0}^{4}x[y]_{y=0}^{y=\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{16}{\int }_{0}^{4}x\sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{16}{\int }_{0}^{4}{x}^{3/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{16}{[\frac{2{x}^{5/2}}{5}]}_{0}^{4} \\  & =\frac{3}{16}\cdot \frac{64}{5} \\  & =\frac{12}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
